description: Policies chosen in one chock selection, packaged as one plugin. Friction, not a security boundary.
disclaimer: These policies add friction to an agent's mistakes; they are not a security boundary.

tier_fail_mode.open: a hook error lets the action through
tier_fail_mode.closed: a hook error blocks the action
tier_fail_mode.configurable: what a hook error does is configurable

steps.note: Both commands are safe to repeat. The plugin loads in place from the directory: restart the Claude Code session, or run /reload-plugins in it, to pick up a rebuild.

remove.note: Delete the build folder __PLUGIN_DIR__: `chock bundle status` lists a build for as long as its folder exists.

Only if no other chock build for this agent is still installed (every chock build made with the marketplace name __MARKETPLACE__ shares it, so removing it takes their registration too): `claude plugin marketplace remove __MARKETPLACE__`. Otherwise leave it registered.

steps.note: Then install __PLUGIN__ from the __MARKETPLACE__ marketplace in /plugins, and review and trust its hooks in /hooks: until you do, they do not run.
Cursor loads __PLUGIN_DIR__ as a local plugin: run "Developer: Reload Window" (or restart Cursor), then check it under Customize. There is no command to run.

remove.note: Delete the build folder __PLUGIN_DIR__ (Cursor loads it from there), then run "Developer: Reload Window" (or restart Cursor). `chock bundle status` lists a build for as long as its folder exists.

devin.name: Devin
devin.label_prefix: best-effort, and a hook error lets the action through:

steps.note: On Windows, `devin plugins install --local` creates a symbolic link, so it needs Developer Mode (Settings > System > For developers) or an elevated shell; otherwise it fails with "os error 1314: A required privilege is not held by the client".
The plugin is linked in place: a rebuild applies from the next Devin session.

remove.note: Delete the build folder __PLUGIN_DIR__: `chock bundle status` lists a build for as long as its folder exists.

steps.note: goose discovers __PLUGIN_DIR__ as a user plugin, in every project: start a new goose session. There is no command to run (`goose plugin install` takes a git URL only). To turn it off, add __PLUGIN__ to disabledPlugins in ~/.config/goose/settings.json.

remove.note: Delete the build folder __PLUGIN_DIR__ (goose discovers it there), then start a new goose session. `chock bundle status` lists a build for as long as its folder exists.

steps.note: Plugins are off in grok until enabled, and chock does not edit grok's config: run `grok plugin list` for the name grok gave this plugin (chock expects __PLUGIN__, its folder name; the docs do not say how a plugin with no plugin.json is named), then `grok plugin enable <name>`, or add it to `enabled` under [plugins] in ~/.grok/config.toml, or press Space on it in the Plugins tab. Re-run the install command after a rebuild.

remove.note: Run `grok plugin list` for the name grok gave this plugin, then `grok plugin uninstall <name>`.
Delete the build folder __PLUGIN_DIR__: `chock bundle status` lists a build for as long as its folder exists.

steps.note: Antigravity 2.0 and the IDE read plugin folders from ~/.gemini/config/plugins/ instead: copy __PLUGIN_DIR__ there. Its hooks name __PLUGIN_DIR__ by absolute path (Antigravity documents no plugin-root variable), so keep that folder where it is; re-run the install command after a rebuild.

OpenHands loads a local plugin when it starts: run `openhands --plugin __PLUGIN_DIR__`, or add "__PLUGIN_DIR__" to sources under [plugins] in ~/.openhands/config.toml (chock does not edit it). Its hooks name __PLUGIN_DIR__ by absolute path (OpenHands documents no plugin-root variable), so keep that folder where it is; a rebuild applies from the next start.

remove.note: Stop passing `--plugin __PLUGIN_DIR__`, and remove "__PLUGIN_DIR__" from sources under [plugins] in ~/.openhands/config.toml if you added it (chock does not edit it).
Delete the build folder __PLUGIN_DIR__: `chock bundle status` lists a build for as long as its folder exists.

steps.note: Kimi Code installs plugins from its TUI only, and chock does not drive it: in Kimi Code run `/plugins install __PLUGIN_DIR__`, then `/reload` (or `/new`). Kimi copies the plugin to $KIMI_CODE_HOME/plugins/managed/__PLUGIN__/ and runs that copy, so after a rebuild install it again. The plugin applies to every project you open (Kimi has no project-level plugin scope); `/plugins disable __PLUGIN__` turns it off.
Run these from the root of the project the plugin is for: `--scope project` records it in that project's Droid settings. The marketplace is local to this machine; chock publishes nothing.

Droid names a local marketplace from its source; if `droid plugin marketplace list` shows a name other than __MARKETPLACE__ (a --dest folder named otherwise), install __PLUGIN__@<that name>. Droid copies the plugin into its cache: after a rebuild run `droid plugin marketplace update` and `droid plugin update __PLUGIN__@__MARKETPLACE__ --scope project`, then start a new session.

remove.note: Run these from the root of the project the plugin was installed for.
Delete the build folder __PLUGIN_DIR__: `chock bundle status` lists a build for as long as its folder exists.

Only if no other chock build for this agent is still installed (every chock build made with the marketplace name __MARKETPLACE__ shares it, so removing it takes their registration too): `droid plugin marketplace remove __MARKETPLACE__`. Otherwise leave it registered.
